title: Standardize header precedence, add scoped project keys and request-signing headers; OpenAI-compat and CORS fixes
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds scoped project API keys (proj_* tokens), canonicalized Authorization header precedence, X-Redwood-Signature/X-Redwood-Nonce request signing headers with deterministic verification, and CORS improvements for browser clients. OpenAI-compat layer now maps legacy headers and preserves streaming semantics. Feature is opt-in for Private/Dedicated via config flags.
description:
Motivation: We have multiple client integrations that rely on different ways of passing credentials (Authorization: Bearer, X-Redwood-Api-Key, project-scoped tokens). This PR unifies header precedence, introduces scoped project keys, and adds simple request-signing primitives to mitigate replay attacks for sensitive admin endpoints. It also fixes several browser CORS issues that caused streaming connections to be preflighted incorrectly and updates the OpenAI-compatibility layer to accept both legacy and canonical headers.

What this changes: 1) Canonical header precedence: Authorization: Bearer (token) > X-Redwood-Api-Key > X-Redwood-Project-Key. Servers now normalize input into a single internal credential object at the earliest request-auth stage. 2) Scoped project keys: new token prefix 'proj_' and minimal JWT-like format (header.payload.sig) carrying project_id and allowlist metadata. Tokens are compatible with existing account tokens but can be scoped and revoked independently. 3) Request signing: optional headers X-Redwood-Nonce and X-Redwood-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 over canonicalized request line + headers + body) plus a deterministic canonicalization routine. Verified in the auth middleware with strict replay-window configurable via env. 4) OpenAI-compat: map Authorization and X-Redwood-Api-Key into the same flow; preserve existing streaming chunking for SSE and streaming HTTP so third-party tools (curl, openai SDKs) behave as before. 5) CORS: add Access-Control-Allow-Headers entries for X-Redwood-Signature and X-Redwood-Nonce, ensure preflight early-return for streaming endpoints to avoid buffering. 6) Observability: add telemetry flags for which credential type was used (account/scoped/project), and metrics when request-signing verification fails.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2394) - [x] Unit tests for token parsing and precedence - [x] Integration tests for CORS and streaming - [x] Compatibility tests against OpenAI-compat shim - [x] Docs update and migration notes - [x] Security review (SEC-112)

Compatibility notes: The change is non-breaking by default. Existing account tokens continue to work. Scoped project tokens are opt-in; customers can create proj_* tokens in Console. Request-signing is opt-in per-route; default replay-window is 2 minutes. Operators on Private/Dedicated can toggle canonicalization lenience for older clients.

Backwards-compatibility mapping examples: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" remains canonical. Older clients sending X-Redwood-Api-Key will be accepted and logged as legacy-header usage. The OpenAI-compat endpoint accepts both Authorization and Api-Key headers and translates them to the normalized credential.

Risks and mitigations: - If operators enable strict signing without rolling out client changes, legitimate requests will be rejected; mitigated with a permissive flag and verbose logs for rollout. - Token format change is additive; ensure no leaking of project metadata in logs. All new tokens are audited at issuance time.

References: linear:ENG-2394, security:SEC-112, support:SUP-721. Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2394/auth-header-precedence-and-scoped-keys.

review_thread_summary: Initial review from Ethan noted a potential race in nonce cleanup; added Redis-based TTL and deterministic nonce bucket key. Priya requested clearer telemetry for legacy header usage which was added (auth.credential_source metric). Alex requested an explicit migration section in docs for operators; docs expanded and example curl commands added. After two CI reruns (streaming test flaky) reviewers approved and marked as security-reviewed. Final sign-off from Priya and Alex before merge.
ci_checks_summary: CI: unit (pass), integration (initial fail on streaming tests), lint (pass), security-scan (pass). Integration failure due to test harness buffering; fixed by streaming handshake change and re-run. Final CI green on second run.
notes_for_ops: Operators: to enable scoped tokens set AUTH_ENABLE_SCOPED_KEYS=true and configure token issuer key in secrets (AUTH_SCOPED_ISSUER_KEY). To enable strict signing set AUTH_STRICT_SIGNING=true and SIGNING_REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS=120. For Private installs, older clients can be allowed by setting AUTH_CANONICALIZER_LENIENCE=1. Monitor auth.signing_failure metric for rollout.
